findings.summary: handle_dd_awaiting_gate_wake and load_mutation_receipt remain library-level: no production module outside fleet_graph.self_gate imports the wake handler, and no MCP tool or CLI entry exposes either to the goal-line seat the dd_awaiting_gate fact ignites. Recorded as a note, not a blocker, because the spec's own §8 preamble adjudicates the runner.py wiring as correct ('第三次尝试确实把 deliver_self_gate_decision 接进了 runner.py...缺陷在通用机制不在该单') and both continuous reviews took the same position; the engine-side duty S12.3 actually tightened is wired at the production assembly point (dd_runner.build_pipeline supplies mutation_inputs to the dispatcher).

The mutation gate's cost is unbounded in target count: enumerate_mutation_targets yields every added production .py call site in base..head, and each target re-runs every frozen acceptance command in the one-shot copy. This repo's own dd-acceptance is two commands (uv sync + pytest, then make verify), and a ticket of this size adds hundreds of call sites, so a single final_review stage would serially run hundreds of full acceptance passes under an 1800s-per-command bound. This is what the spec mandates ('逐个删除') and not a deviation, but the spec's cheapness rationale ('跑一个文件而非 2669 条') assumed one small frozen command; flagging the operational scale for the supervisory face before M3 goes live.

The instructed mechanical product-consistency check (git diff between implementation_subject_commit and subject_commit excluding .dev-dispatch) was not executed: this reviewer has only file-inspection tools and no shell or Git access. I instead read the worktree's .git pointer and the linked gitdir's HEAD (0db1b5075f9d11426b99d7a0dc2adda211d1b8e3, equal to subject_commit) and logs/HEAD, which show the review seal stacked on 97c414e8 stacked on the handoff's work_head 78c72d332e. The review was performed against the checked-out product tree at subject_commit and no product discrepancy was observed there, but the diff itself was not run.
